plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like composite flower heads made of golden ray florets surrounding a dark central disc. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, and the plant is widely grown for ornament, seeds, and oil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn in the Northern Hemisphere (July to September)
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated worldwide, especially in the United States, Ukraine, Russia, and Argentina
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds follow the sun from east to west (heliotropism), but mature flower heads typically stop moving and face east, which helps warm them in the morning and attract pollinators.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-green foliage and slender spikes of fragrant purple flowers. It thrives in full sun and well-drained soil and is a favorite of bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August), with peak bloom in July in many regions
plants.location: Native to the western Mediterranean; widely cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: The name lavender likely derives from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', reflecting its long use by Romans in bathing and laundry.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.commonName: African Lily / Lily of the Nile
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial with strap-like leaves and tall, leafless stems topped with rounded umbels of trumpet-shaped blue flowers. It is a popular border and container plant in warm climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Northern Hemisphere (July to September); in its native range it blooms in the southern summer
plants.location: Native to South Africa; widely grown in coastal California, the Mediterranean, Australia, and the UK
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, Agapanthus is not a true lily; its name comes from the Greek 'agape' (love) and 'anthos' (flower).

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy prairie perennial with drooping pinkish-purple petals around a prominent spiny, orange-brown central cone. It is a magnet for bees, butterflies, and seed-eating goldfinches, and tolerates heat and drought.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (June to October), with strong bloom in August
plants.location: Native to eastern and central North America; grown in gardens across temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: The genus name Echinacea comes from the Greek 'echinos', meaning hedgehog, referring to the spiny central cone of the flower.
